lead: You don’t need to automate your whole business. You need one task: the one that takes time every week, feels tedious, and won’t cause damage if it goes wrong. In this lesson, AI interviews you about your week and makes a list; you choose the first task.
objetivo: make a list of your repetitive tasks and choose the first one for the agent: lots of time, lots of boredom, low risk.

aprende.t: List what you repeat every week
Rate the time, boredom, and risk
Set aside anything that affects money or clients

hero_alt: Man around 45, sitting at a table at night, checking items on a paper task list; a laptop and a mug beside him.

secoes.titulo: From a packed week to the first task
secoes.sub: Click each step to see what happens.

nos.detalhe: AI asks one question at a time: what do you do on the computer that feels tedious, which websites do you visit every week, what do you copy from one place to another, which numbers do you pull together, and what do you put together when a new client comes in.
Each task becomes a line with the apps it uses, how many minutes per week it takes, and how boring it is. Make an honest estimate: the exact number doesn't matter, but the order does.

itens.t: money or a customer = medium at minimum

nos.detalhe: Risk is the damage if the agent makes a mistake. Reading and summarizing is low risk. Anything that affects money or involves talking to a customer starts at medium, even if it seems simple.

itens.t: lots of time + lots of boredom + low risk

nos.detalhe: The agent's first task is the one at the top of the list: the one that combines the most minutes and the most boredom with low risk. The others can wait until later, one at a time.

secoes.legenda: One new task per week, never several at once (lesson 8).

secoes.titulo: How to rate tasks without getting stuck

texto: Add up the time: 15 minutes a day, five days a week, is 75 minutes per week.
A 5-minute task once a month is rarely worth the work of setting up an agent.

exemplo.texto: Copying orders from WhatsApp into a spreadsheet: 20 min a day, 100 min a week.

texto: 5 is a task you put off. 1 is one you even enjoy doing.
A boring task is one you do in a rush, and rushing leads to mistakes: delegating can also improve quality.

passos.sub: the damage a mistake could cause
texto: Low: the agent only reads and writes a draft for you. Medium: it changes a record or company spreadsheet, or prepares a message for a customer. High: it pays, sends, deletes, or signs.
In this course, high risk always stays with you: the agent prepares it, you carry it out.
Start now: one task, the best one on the list. Later: the good tasks that can wait their turn. Do not delegate: anything high-risk or that depends on your judgment.
If you're unsure between two tasks, choose the one with lower risk.

secoes.sub: Copy and paste this into a new ChatGPT or Claude conversation. Take your time answering the questions.

blocos.rot: In chat · find the boring task
blocos.conteudo:
Help me find the computer task I should hand over to an AI agent first.

Ask me these questions ONE AT A TIME and wait for my answer:
1. What’s a typical week like for me? What do I do on the computer that’s boring or repetitive?
2. Which websites, systems, or apps do I use every week?
3. What do I copy from one place and paste into another?
4. Which numbers or reports do I put together every week?
5. When a new client comes in, what do I need to enter or prepare, and in which tools?

Then make a list with ONE LINE PER TASK, in this format:
N | task | apps | X min | boredom N | low/medium/high risk | start now / later / do not delegate

Rules:
- Any task that involves money or talks to a client is at least medium risk.
- Paying, sending, deleting, or signing is high risk and must be marked "do not delegate".
- Only ONE line can say "start now": the task that combines the most minutes and the most boredom with low risk.
- Sort from the best first task to the worst.

At the end, write: "Your first task is ___" and a paragraph saying what goes in (where the data comes from), what comes out (what I receive), and how often. I’ll use that paragraph in the agent sheet.

blocos.rot: Example of a finished list (a custom furniture store)
blocos.conteudo:
1 | Weekly website report for your business partner | Search Console (Google’s free dashboard), spreadsheet | 60 min | boredom 5 | low risk | start now
2 | Copy quotes from email to the spreadsheet | Gmail, spreadsheet | 90 min | boredom 4 | medium risk | later
3 | Enter supplier invoices in accounts payable | email, spreadsheet | 45 min | boredom 5 | medium risk | later
4 | Set up a folder and schedule for the new client | Drive, spreadsheet | 40 min | boredom 3 | medium risk | later
5 | Pay suppliers | banking app | 30 min | boredom 3 | high risk | do not delegate

abas.html:
1. The list has at least 5 lines, one per task.
  2. Every line has minutes, boredom, risk, and a decision.
  3. Only one line says start now, and its risk is low.
  4. Paying, sending, or deleting is marked do not delegate.

In Claude Code or Codex, use the same prompt: open a terminal in a new folder (for example, my-agents), run claude or codex, paste the prompt, and at the end ask it to save the list in tasks.md. Starting with lesson 2, that folder will hold your agent sheets.

• Choosing the hardest task to "test the AI": the first task needs to go well, not impress.
  • Choosing the rarest task: it takes months to trust an agent with a monthly task.
  • Marking a message to a customer as low risk: once a wrong message is sent, you can't take it back.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Which of these is the best first task for an agent?
opcoes: Reply to customer complaints on WhatsApp on its own, without you reviewing them.
Summarize the website numbers every Monday in a report for you to read.
perguntas.explica: Summarizing something for you to read is low risk, happens every week, and is boring. Replying to a client and paying a bill are medium or high risk; the year’s strategy is rare and depends on your judgment.

perguntas.p: A task prepares a payment reminder for a customer but doesn’t send it. What’s the risk?
opcoes: At least medium: it involves money and a customer, even as a draft.
It depends only on how many minutes of your work time it takes each week.
perguntas.explica: Money or customer-related tasks start at medium risk, even as a draft, because an incorrect text approved in a hurry goes out with your name on it. Risk is high when the agent pays, sends, or deletes.

perguntas.p: Why does only one task get "start now"?
opcoes: Because chat only allows one agent sheet per account, and the second one erases the first from memory.
Because you need to check everything the agent does at first, and you can only manage that with one task.
Because the other tasks can never be delegated.
Because the light model can only do one task per week.
perguntas.explica: At first, you check every result. With one task, that fits into your week; with five, you stop checking and mistakes slip through. The others can wait their turn: add one new task per week, as the plan in lesson 8 shows.

perguntas.p: The task "copy orders to the spreadsheet" takes 20 minutes a day, five days a week. How many minutes per week go on the list?
opcoes: 20 min, the time it takes for one day
perguntas.explica: 20 minutes times 5 days is 100 minutes a week. A common mistake is to write down just one day's time and underestimate the task.

itens.texto: Don't automate everything: choose the task that adds up to the most time and boredom, with low risk.
Money or a client starts at medium risk; you handle payments, sending, deleting, and signing.
The other tasks can wait their turn. Add one new task per week, never several at once.
